title: Learning when responsibility arrives
literal_meaning: When it falls on the shoulder, one learns to play.
explanation: Taking responsibility can force a beginner to learn the necessary skill. The compressed wording leaves the instrument unnamed; imagining a carried percussion instrument helps explain the metaphor, but does not establish which instrument first inspired it. This is encouragement to learn through doing, not a guarantee that preparation is unnecessary.
meaning_odia: ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ କାନ୍ଧରେ ପଡ଼ିଲେ ତାହା ସମ୍ଭାଳିବାର ଉପାୟ ଶିଖିବାକୁ ହୁଏ—ଏହି ଭାବ କଥାଟିରେ ଅଛି। ଦୂରରୁ ଦେଖିବା ଓ ନିଜେ କାମରେ ହାତ ଦେବାର ଅନୁଭବ ଏକ ନୁହେଁ। ଏହା କାମ କରି ଶିଖିବାର କଥା; ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତି କିମ୍ବା ଅନ୍ୟର ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ଅନାବଶ୍ୟକ ବୋଲି କହେନାହିଁ।
usage_example: A first-time organiser worries about arranging a neighbourhood reading session. A more experienced friend uses the saying while offering help with the practical tasks. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The body carrying a burden and the hands learning a performance meet in one image. No historical link to a named musical tradition has been verified.

title: Complaining while collecting
literal_meaning: Keep crying; tie up whatever you receive.
explanation: The complaint continues while the benefits are quietly gathered. Read as irony about dissatisfaction that does not prevent acceptance.
meaning_odia: ମୁହଁରେ ଅସନ୍ତୋଷ ଚାଲିଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ ମିଳୁଥିବା ଲାଭକୁ ଛାଡ଼ିବାର ଇଚ୍ଛା ନାହିଁ। ଅଭିଯୋଗ ଓ ଗ୍ରହଣ କରିବାର ଏହି ଯୁଗଳ ଆଚରଣକୁ କଥାଟି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ କରେ। କହୁଥିବା କଥା ସହ କରୁଥିବା କାମକୁ ମେଳାଇ ଦେଖିଲେ ଏହାର ମଜା ବୁଝାପଡ଼େ।
usage_example: A guest calls every gift inadequate but carefully packs them all to take home. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: Tying things into a bundle supplies the image. This interpretation is editorial; the witness provides no gloss.

title: Tears that conceal support
odia: ଚୋର ମା ଯଦି କାନ୍ଦେ ଆଖି ମଳିମଳି କାନ୍ଦେ ।
literal_meaning: If the thief’s mother cries, she cries rubbing her eyes.
explanation: The source reads the display of distress as concealed support for a wrongdoer. The charge is complicity behind appearances, not proof that a crying relative is guilty.
meaning_odia: ଦୁଃଖ ପ୍ରକାଶ କରୁଥିବା ଲୋକର ନିଜର ସମ୍ପୃକ୍ତି ଗୋପନ ରହିଛି—ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଏହି ବିରୋଧାଭାସକୁ ଧରେ। ବାହାରର କାନ୍ଦଣା ଓ ଭିତରର ଜାଣିବା ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଫାଙ୍କ ଥିଲେ କଥାଟି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ ହୋଇଉଠେ। କିନ୍ତୁ କାନ୍ଦୁଥିବା ଲୋକ ବା ଅଭିଯୁକ୍ତଙ୍କ ଆତ୍ମୀୟ ହେବା ନିଜେ ଦୋଷର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
usage_example: Someone publicly deplores a friend’s deception while privately helping conceal it. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The maternal figure belongs to the saying; responsibility cannot be inferred from kinship or tears alone.

title: From scarcity into famine
literal_meaning: To go from high prices into famine.
explanation: A change meant to escape difficulty leads into something worse. Here କାନ୍ତାର is the dictionary’s famine sense, not its separate forest sense.
meaning_odia: ଦରବୃଦ୍ଧିର ଅସୁବିଧାରୁ ବଞ୍ଚିବାକୁ ଯାଇ ଦୁର୍ଭିକ୍ଷ ପରି ଆହୁରି ବଡ଼ କଷ୍ଟରେ ପଡ଼ିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଏହା। ଉତ୍ସର ଏହି ପ୍ରୟୋଗରେ ‘କାନ୍ତାର’ର ଅର୍ଥ ଦୁର୍ଭିକ୍ଷ, ବଣ ନୁହେଁ। ଗୋଟିଏ ଅସୁବିଧା ଏଡ଼ାଇବାର ବାଟ ବାଛିବା ବେଳେ ନୂଆ ବାଟର ବିପଦ ବି ଦେଖିବାକୁ ହୁଏ।
usage_example: A shop changes to a cheaper supplier, then loses more because deliveries repeatedly fail. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)

title: Keep clear of a known danger
odia: ଅରଣା ମଇଁଷି ରହିଛି ଅନାଇ, ମଇଁଷିର ପାଖ ନଯାଅ ଦନାଇ ।
literal_meaning: The untamed buffalo stands watching; do not go near it, Danai.
explanation: The warning makes caution concrete: noticing a danger should change how close one goes to it. This is a bounded editorial reading of the warning, not a documented account of an encounter.
meaning_odia: ବିପଦ ସାମ୍ନାରେ ଦିଶୁଛି, ତେଣୁ ଆଉ ପାଖକୁ ନଯିବାକୁ ସତର୍କ କରାଯାଉଛି। ମଇଁଷିର ଚିତ୍ର ଦେଇ କେବଳ ବିପଦ ଚିହ୍ନିବା ନୁହେଁ, ତାହା ଅନୁସାରେ ପଦକ୍ଷେପ ବଦଳାଇବା କଥା ବୁଝିହେବ। ଏହା ସତର୍କବାଣୀର ଏକ ସୀମିତ ପାଠ, ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ଘଟଣାର ବିବରଣୀ ନୁହେଁ।
usage_example: A worker notices an unstable stack and keeps others away until it is secured. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: ଦନାଇ occurs as an address in the line. The source gives no biographical evidence or authorship proof for this name.

title: A fine shawl and forgotten faces
literal_meaning: Is this the former Kahnei? With a fine soft shawl on the shoulder, does he recognise people?
explanation: The question contrasts a remembered person with the way he now behaves. The fine shawl becomes the visible sign beside a failure to recognise others. Our reading hears a teasing accusation that improved appearance or standing has brought social distance. The line does not tell us that the cloth itself changes character, or that everyone whose circumstances improve becomes proud. Its force is directed at the particular person being addressed through this pointed question.
meaning_odia: ଏ କି ସେଇ ପୂର୍ବର କହ୍ନେଇ—ପ୍ରଶ୍ନରେ ପୁରୁଣା ପରିଚୟ ଓ ଏବର ଆଚରଣ ମୁହାଁମୁହିଁ ହେଉଛି। କାନ୍ଧର ସରୁ କୋମଳ ଚାଦର ପାଖରେ ମଣିଷ ନ ଚିହ୍ନିବାର କଥା ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ବେଶ ବା ସ୍ଥିତି ବଦଳିଲା ପରେ ପୁରୁଣା ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ଅବହେଳା କରିବା ଉପରେ କଟାକ୍ଷ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। ପୋଷାକଟି ନିଜେ ଦୋଷୀ ନୁହେଁ; ତାହା ପିନ୍ଧିଥିବା ଲୋକର ବ୍ୟବହାର ପ୍ରଶ୍ନରେ ପଡ଼ୁଛି।
english_summary: A changed appearance becomes an image for forgetting familiar people.
odia_summary: ବେଶ ବଦଳିଲା ପରେ ପରିଚିତ ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ଭୁଲିବାରେ କଟାକ୍ଷ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: After a promotion, a friend stops greeting the people who used to share lunch with him. One of them quotes the saying in a private conversation, teasing the new distance rather than the friend’s clothes.
cultural_context: The source labels the headword Jajpur; no exclusive origin follows. Kahnei remains the name in the quotation, not an identified deity or historical person. Fine soft cloth is explicit; fibre, cost and status-history are not established. Source spelling ପୂରୂବ retained.
